title: PowerPoint on Windows: Copilot agent notifies you when work finishes or needs attention
summary: Hold: the briefing assigns an add-on licensing model and restricts the audience to licensed users without establishing which agent the desktop notification feature uses. The roadmap facts and existing control paths are supported, but licensing from the separate PowerPoint Agents documentation must remain background rather than a requirement for this feature.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[1].governs; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The related Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents documentation requires a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents are premium capabilities available only to users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Those documented agents are not available to Copilot Chat users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: The agents aren't available to Copilot Chat users who don't have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: The Copilot overview describes the full Microsoft 365 Copilot experience as add-on licensed.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not identify this desktop notification agent as the separately documented PowerPoint Agent or publish an entitlement specific to notifications.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint agent" "notifications" license credits; "PowerPoint" "agent" "Windows" licence notifications. Read roadmap, wordexcelppt-agents and copilot-overview; the agents page describes agents in the Microsoft Copilot app, not desktop PowerPoint asynchronous notifications.

claims.claim: This notification capability has an add-on licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint agent" "notifications" license credits; "PowerPoint" "agent" "Windows" licence notifications. Read wordexcelppt-agents and copilot-overview; neither establishes an add-on requirement for this item, and the overview also documents in-app access without the add-on.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "unknown". Keep the existing notes and Cost and licensing paragraph describing the paid licence as background for the separate Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents. Replace the cost rationale with "Low. Plan for pilot checks and support communications; licensing and any charge or meter specific to notifications are not yet published."

claims.claim: Anthropic models must be enabled for the separately documented Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents to work.
claims.quote: These agents exclusively use Anthropic's AI models. This AI model must be enabled.

claims.claim: No automation for the Microsoft 365 Anthropic subprocessor availability setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors Anthropic enable disable Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; "Anthropic" "subprocessor" "Graph" API settings. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor and returned configuration excerpts; only admin UI steps describe this setting.

claims.claim: Anthropic can be disabled at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > User access > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor.
claims.quote: On the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors page, under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor.
claims.fix: Use the full path "Copilot > Settings > User access > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor" in controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table. The omitted step is a heading, not a navigation choice.

claims.claim: Changing Anthropic availability requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.claim: Disabling Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor removes users' option to use Claude models, rather than affecting PowerPoint alone.
claims.quote: Once you disable Anthropic as an AI subprocessor, users won't have the option to use Claude models.

claims.claim: A user's licences are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
